Abstract

Motivation
Phylogenetic placement workflows often depend on carefully curated reference sets and can become difficult to scale when the number of candidate sequences grows quickly. In metagenomic and cancer-related analyses, this creates a need for methods that reduce manual curation while preserving taxonomic or clade-level resolution.

Results
We introduce a hybrid clustering framework that builds compact reference panels from sequence collections and supports placement against layered phylogenetic backbones. The approach combines automated representative selection with a preprocessing stage for large batches of query sequences. Benchmarks on simulated and empirical datasets indicate improved throughput and stable placement accuracy across nested reference structures.

Availability and implementation
Source code is freely available under GPLv3 from a public repository.

Supplementary information
Supplementary data are available online.

Abstract

Motivation
Phylogenetic placement pipelines often rely on carefully curated reference collections and can become hard to scale as candidate sequence counts increase rapidly. In metagenomic and cancer-related studies, this creates a need for approaches that reduce manual curation while maintaining taxonomic or clade-level resolution.

Results
We present a hybrid clustering framework that constructs compact reference panels from sequence collections and enables placement against layered phylogenetic backbones. The method pairs automated representative selection with a preprocessing stage for large batches of query sequences. Benchmarks on simulated and empirical datasets show improved throughput and consistent placement accuracy across nested reference structures.
